ui_bugs.issue: NEW crash (progression from iteration_16's fixed bug, same call site): TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match') at `new _UniformGroup` -> `new Shader` -> `new _Filter` -> `_Filter.from` -> `PixiRenderer._makeLitFilter` -> `_buildNormalLitSystem` -> `_buildLayers`. Full-screen 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay appears the instant gameplay canvas initializes (same UX impact as iteration_16's crash -- game is unplayable). This is thrown while PixiJS's `_UniformGroup` constructor tries to introspect each uniform's `type` string (e.g. via regex on the type descriptor) to determine its GPU layout, and something in the `resources` object passed to Filter.from is malformed for PixiJS v8's expected shape. Most likely root cause: the `resources` block in `_makeLitFilter()` nests uniforms under a wrapper key `uLight: { uLightPos: {...}, uLightColor: {...}, ... }` and textures under `extraTextures: { uNormalTexture: ... }` -- PixiJS v8's Filter.from() `resources` map convention typically expects either (a) a flat map of uniform-name -> {value,type} pairs plus texture-name -> Texture/TextureSource directly (no extra wrapper keys), or (b) resources organized as named UniformGroup instances built via `new UniformGroup({...})`, not raw nested objects. As currently written, PixiJS likely tries to treat the top-level keys 'extraTextures' and 'uLight' themselves as single uniforms/resources, and when it reaches into e.g. 'uLight' expecting a `.type` string to regex-match against, it's undefined, hence `undefined.match(...)`.

Recommend flattening resources to match PixiJS v8's documented custom-filter resource format exactly -- e.g. `resources: { uNormalTexture: this.normalTex.source, uLightPos: { value: [0,0], type: 'vec2<f32>' }, uLightColor: {...}, uLightRadius: {...}, uAmbient: {...}, uObjSize: {...} }` (no 'extraTextures'/'uLight' wrapper keys), or explicitly construct a `new UniformGroup({...})` and pass that as a named resource per PixiJS v8 Filter examples.

Strongly recommend wrapping the Filter.from()/_buildNormalLitSystem() call in a try/catch with a safe fallback (skip lit-sprite rendering, fall back to old flat-fill) so that a shader/resource construction failure in this experimental feature does not take down the ENTIRE game/app again -- this is the second consecutive pass where this exact code path has thrown an uncaught, app-breaking exception. This was flagged in iteration_16's review too.

Once the resources shape is fixed and a fresh session reaches gameplay without the overlay, the full visual verification suite (lit player body across aim angles, muzzle-flash brightening, lit hydropistol bullets, confirm old lighting fully removed, basic smoke test) still needs to be run from scratch -- none of it was reachable this pass either.
critical_code_review_comments: The specific fix described in the request (adding `vertex: defaultFilterVert` to `_makeLitFilter`'s `gl` block) is verified present in pixiRenderer.js line 338 and DID resolve the originally reported crash -- confirmed by the fact the error stack now progresses one level deeper (from GlProgram/ensurePrecision into UniformGroup/Shader construction) before failing.

The new failure is in the exact same function (_makeLitFilter, lines 336-351) at the `resources:` block -- this strongly suggests the resources object shape (nested `extraTextures`/`uLight` wrapper keys) doesn't match what PixiJS v8's Filter.from() convenience API expects for auto-building UniformGroups/textures from a resources map.

No defensive try/catch exists anywhere around _buildNormalLitSystem()/_makeLitFilter(), so any future shader/resource construction issue will continue to crash the entire app -- this exact concern was already raised in iteration_16's review and remains unaddressed.

_updateLitUniforms (line 357-364) reads `filter.resources.uLight.uniforms` -- this confirms the developer's intent was indeed a nested 'uLight' uniform group, so the fix here likely needs `new UniformGroup({...})` explicitly constructed and passed as the 'uLight' resource, rather than a raw plain object, per PixiJS v8's Filter/Shader resource conventions (Filter.from's resources map expects either UniformGroup instances or auto-generated single uniforms directly at the top level, not arbitrarily-named plain-object groupings).

rca of the issue: Root cause: PixiJS v8's Filter.from()/Shader construction pipeline builds UniformGroup instances from the `resources` object passed in. The current _makeLitFilter() code nests its uniforms under an arbitrary wrapper key `uLight: { uLightPos: {...}, uLightColor: {...}, uLightRadius: {...}, uAmbient: {...}, uObjSize: {...} }` and its texture under `extraTextures: { uNormalTexture: this.normalTex.source }`. When PixiJS's internal `new _UniformGroup(...)` constructor iterates the resources map trying to auto-detect each entry's WGSL/GLSL type via a type-string regex `.match(...)`, it appears to hit the outer wrapper key(s) themselves (which have no `.type` property, being plain nested objects rather than {value,type} uniform descriptors or Texture instances) and calls `.match()` on `undefined`. This is consistent with `_updateLitUniforms()` elsewhere in the file expecting to read back `filter.resources.uLight.uniforms` -- confirming the intent was a named UniformGroup called 'uLight', which needs to be constructed explicitly via PixiJS's `UniformGroup` class (imported from 'pixi.js') rather than passed as a raw plain object literal. Mitigation: (1) flatten resources to top-level {value,type} uniform entries + direct texture-source entries matching PixiJS v8's Filter.from() convenience API exactly, OR (2) explicitly `import { UniformGroup } from 'pixi.js'` and construct `new UniformGroup({...}, false)` for the light-uniforms group, passing that as the 'uLight' resource entry, and continuing to pass the normal-map texture source directly (not nested under 'extraTextures') as a separate top-level resource key like 'uNormalTexture'. Recommend also adding a try/catch around _buildNormalLitSystem() with a safe non-lit fallback so any future construction issue in this experimental feature doesn't crash the whole app again.
